note: Adapted from Light & Wilson's 1936 original description (in English), original name Nasutitermes latus, new species; no alate found, only the soldier; because the original printing and scan are poor and the soldier measurement table is entirely garbled, only the readable descriptive text is used and no measurements are listed. Type locality Sir J. Brooke Point, Palawan, Philippines.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier close to N. luzonicus and N. simulans, but the head is broader overall and the front of the head broadly flattened, so that the antennal fossae are visible from above; nasus shorter, narrower at the base and more pointed at the tip, head higher, the nasus elevation lower, abdomen short and thick. It differs from N. javanicus as N. simulans differs from that species.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier: head chestnut; base of the nasus dull smoke-coloured, the tip pale red; antennae pale red at the base grading to yellow at the tip; tergites and sclerites smoke-brown, the pronotum darkest; sternites very pale brown; the rest pale yellow. Head and nasus shaped as figured: nasus short and blunt, relatively narrow at the base; nasus elevation low but distinct; head broad, widest at the antennal insertions; antennal fossae visible from above; 3—4 scattered long fine hairs on the head. Antennae 13-segmented, segments 4 and 5 the shortest and about equal, segment 3 longer. Abdomen relatively short and broad, slightly convex. Measurements: the original measurement table is damaged in the scan, so no values are listed.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Alate: unknown. Distribution and biology: a single collection (Sir J. Brooke Point, Palawan, collected by E. H. Taylor), taken from rotten wood; the remaining habits unknown.
